issues.body: decompose_run() includes any job whose conclusion is not null, cancelled, or skipped. This admits failure, timed_out, action_required, and other non-success outcomes. Such jobs can terminate before later steps execute, producing truncated totals and incomplete step inventories; including them in per-leg medians can understate runtime, distort imbalance and fold recommendations, and omit slow steps. The test named test_incomplete_jobs_are_excluded_from_the_sample still covers only cancelled, skipped, and running jobs, so it cannot detect this case.
issues.fix_hint: Restrict topology-steering observations to jobs whose conclusion is exactly "success". If non-success jobs are useful diagnostically, keep them in a separate population that cannot affect aggregation or derived findings. Add a fixture with successful observations plus a short failed job and assert the failed job is excluded from decompose_run()/collect_fixture aggregation.
issues.title: Failed jobs still contaminate representative timing observations

verdict.summary: Round 4's major measurement-validity defect remains unchanged. decompose_run() still accepts every conclusion except null, cancelled, and skipped, so failed, timed-out, action-required, and other non-success jobs can enter medians and topology recommendations despite potentially truncated durations and step inventories. The fixture test still omits a failed-job counterexample. Progress is therefore stagnant.
